newsitem.title: USA: Money managers cautious on U.S. debt -- survey.
newsitem.headline: Money managers cautious on U.S. debt -- survey.

text.p: U.S. money managers engaged in defensive positioning of their debt portfolios over the past week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"There was very clear movement toward more defensive positions over the past week with significant movement along the curve," the report said.
The movement along the curve was more pronounced among larger portfolios, according to the report.
"The increased caution that has been apparent since (Federal Reserve Chairman) Alan Greenspan's 'irrational exuberance' comment has been taken to another level," the report said.

In the week ended January 7, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading fell to 4.94 from 5.10 the prior week; the asset-weighted number rose to 5.46 from 5.27 in the week ended December 31, according to the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio dropped to 6.45 percent from 6.56 percent.
Duration bogey slipped to 4.20 from 4.22 on an arithmetic basis and held steady at 4.93 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
Sixteen percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from eight percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active fell to 4.75 from 5.0 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
